VALUE: The package targets SDMX 2.0, where the formal term for a Data Structure Definition is Key Family. The principles define dimensions, time dimension, primary measure and attributes as DSD / Key Family components.
Guidelines for the Design of Data Structure Definitions

The supplied principles require DSDs to start from the statistical observation, use TIME_PERIOD instead of year columns, use OBS_VALUE as the primary measure, and attach attributes at the highest level at which they are constant.
Per-report artifacts cite the glossary for cross-domain concept reuse including REF_AREA examples and OBS_STATUS with codelist ID CL_OBS_STATUS.

The supplied evidence confirms that the SDMX Global Registry provides a codelist catalogue. Exact versions and detailed contents for CL_FREQ, CL_SEX, CL_OBS_STATUS, CL_SEASONAL_ADJUST and unit codelists were not supplied.
The principles identify FREQ as a usual dimension and recommend SDMX CL_FREQ where compatible. Annual, quarterly and monthly frequency are required across the source reports.

The principles identify SEX as a dimension when sex disaggregation is present and state that SDMX CL_SEX exists. Source labels include Women/Men/Total and Female/Male/Total, but exact code mappings were not confirmed.

The supplied glossary evidence states that Observation Status has concept ID OBS_STATUS and codelist ID CL_OBS_STATUS. Mappings for source values such as Final, Provisional, Estimated, Forecast and Observed require governance.
The source guidance identifies UNESCO ISCED as the education-level classification source to check. The education report says education-level labels require ISCED mapping review.
Per-report evidence confirms UN M49 country and area code examples, but the report areas Northland, Centralia and South Coast are synthetic/local and no authoritative UN M49 mapping is confirmed.
The prices and consumption report references consumption divisions resembling COICOP, but no supplied evidence confirms the revision or exact mapping.
Urban and rural residence categories in the household spending report are not confirmed to follow degree-of-urbanisation semantics, so DEG_URB remains only a candidate source.

This aggregate covers example_01_labour_market.pdf, example_02_health_system.pdf, example_03_education.pdf, example_04_agriculture.pdf and example_05_prices_consumption.pdf as a reusable cross-report DSD design, not as visual report layouts.
Exact versions and code contents for candidate SDMX codelists such as CL_FREQ, CL_SEX, CL_OBS_STATUS, CL_SEASONAL_ADJUST and unit codelists were not confirmed from supplied evidence.
Synthetic/local geographies such as Northland, Centralia and South Coast are treated with a shared local area codelist where used; no UN M49 or ISO 3166 mapping is confirmed.
Local industry aggregates in the labour vacancy structure are not confirmed ISIC categories and must not be silently mapped to ISIC.
Health cause-of-death labels resemble broad cause families, but no ICD version is confirmed; cause is represented by a local broad cause codelist.
Education-level labels require ISCED review; EDUCATION_LEVEL is represented by a local education-level codelist pending authoritative mapping.
Crop names require agricultural classification review; common crop labels are retained in a local crop codelist until mapping is confirmed.
Fertilizer products are local market categories and are not verified CPC or other product-classification codes.
Consumption divisions are not mapped to COICOP because the report explicitly says the revision is not confirmed.
Wealth and expenditure quintiles are survey-specific and are not silently mapped to standard income or distribution classifications.

The education and prices/consumption reports do not state a reference area or country, so REF_AREA is not included in those structures; geographic scope should be handled in reference metadata or added to future structures if supplied.
The local currencies used for fertilizer prices and household spending are deliberately unnamed, so no ISO 4217 currency code can be assigned from report evidence.

Publication title, file name, pages, methodology narratives, caveats, source URLs, contacts and revision-policy text are intentionally not modelled as DSD dimensions; they belong in MSD / Metadata Set or provenance layers.
Observation status/source-status mappings such as Final, Provisional, Estimated, Forecast, Observed and Modelled estimate require code-level governance before automated SDMX exchange.

The source value Survey estimate is treated as a dataset-level estimation-type qualifier, not as OBS_STATUS, because it describes the data source/estimation nature and is constant across displayed household observations.

Ten Key Families are retained because the accepted and new report artifacts represent ten distinct observation grains with materially different measures, populations, sources, units, classifications, frequencies or attribute attachment levels: quarterly unemployment rates; monthly job vacancy counts; annual registered death counts; annual hospital-bed stock counts; annual education enrollment headcounts; annual lower-secondary completion rates; annual crop harvested area and production indicators; monthly fertilizer retail prices; monthly CPI index values; and annual mean household spending. Shared cross-domain components are reused consistently where meanings are equivalent, including FREQ, TIME_PERIOD, OBS_VALUE, UNIT_MEASURE, OBS_STATUS, SEX and REF_AREA with a common synthetic area codelist. Local classifications are kept separate where semantics or versions differ, such as CROP, PRODUCT, CONSUMPTION_DIVISION, EDUCATION_LEVEL, CAUSE_OF_DEATH, ACTIVITY, OWNERSHIP, WEALTH_QUINTILE and EXPENDITURE_QUINTILE. The structures are not merged into a single generic indicator DSD because that would introduce many non-applicable dimensions and obscure differences in statistical population, source methodology, unit, classification version and qualifier attachment levels.
